license_or_model: GPL-3.0; plugins/add-ons may have individual licenses
sdlc_model: Documented hybrid process: Moodle HQ stable teams explicitly use Scrum; the wider project uses tracker-based integration, peer review, testing, weekly releases, and stable maintenance.
requirements_evidence: Roadmaps are curated during quarterly planning for a rolling 12–18 months. Inputs include tracker requests/votes, forums, Product Advisory Groups, staff, and community feedback. Bugs/features enter the tracker and are triaged; major features receive product-team specifications.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Official architecture documentation describes a PHP web application with database/file store, modular core-plus-plugin architecture, plugin APIs, upgradeability goals, and single-server or separated/load-balanced deployment. Development documentation describes UX/specification work and iterative design/implementation in sprints.
implementation_evidence: Every core fix/new feature must have a Tracker issue. Contributors publish branches; patches are peer-reviewed, discussed, integrated, tested, and released. New features use main; fixes are backported to supported maintenance branches.
testing_evidence: Layered QA includes developer/peer/integration testing, PHPUnit, Behat, CI checks, daily regression builds, JMeter performance testing, browser testing, and a 4–6 week volunteer QA cycle for major releases.
release_or_operations_evidence: Weekly integration/release workflow; code freeze, beta/RC tags, package publication, QA preparation, and post-release synchronization. Major releases occur every six months; point releases every two months.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Responsible disclosure, restricted Tracker handling, security-team triage, fixes/testing, CVEs, packages, advisories, coordinated disclosure, backports, and supported-branch maintenance are documented.
limitations: No single formal SDLC label for the whole project; architecture page is older/read-only; public evidence is stronger for core development than deployment monitoring, incident response, plugin practice, or operational SLOs.
sources: requirements, implementation, Scrum, review, testing, release

license_or_model: AGPL-3.0 for openedx-platform; ecosystem licenses vary by repository
sdlc_model: Not explicitly named; documented lifecycle links product proposals/roadmap, design/technical planning, pull-request implementation/review, CI/manual QA, named releases, deployment, and security updates.
requirements_evidence: Product proposals must state overview, user problem, use cases, solution, implementation plan, resources, and long-term ownership/maintenance. Proposals link GitHub issues, undergo cross-organization review, and require consensus or resolution of objections.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Architecture documentation describes LMS/Studio, independently deployed applications, micro-frontends, stable APIs, databases, and background workers. Product/design review requires wireframes, prototypes, final UI, rationale, and technical-deviation documentation.
implementation_evidence: Contribution workflow uses forks, Git, issues, pull requests, Conventional Commits, focused changes, rebase, product review, and core-committer code review.
testing_evidence: GitHub Actions run PR test builds and checks. Documentation requires tests and a manual test plan; Codecov changed-line coverage, pep8/pylint, static analysis, and XSS linting are documented.
release_or_operations_evidence: Named releases are created every six months; community testing lasts two months before availability. edx.org deployment is documented as multiple times daily. Branches/tags and release notes record changes; only the latest release is supported.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Private vulnerability reporting, Security Working Group review/triage, and fixes in the most recent release are documented. Older release lines are not patched under the cited policy.
limitations: No officially named SDLC model; multi-repository ecosystem means practices/licenses/release details vary; public evidence is incomplete for organization-wide traceability, deployment pipelines, SLOs, incident response, and every component’s maintenance policy.

sdlc_model: Not explicitly named; evidence shows community roadmap consultation, Jira intake/requirements, branch/commit/PR review, QA verification, release-manager merging, and maintenance/security releases.
requirements_evidence: Community roadmap process defines a three-year roadmap through consultation, working-group feedback, and adoption. Jira tracks bugs, suggestions, tasks, and contributions; feature issues are expected to include use cases and detailed requirements.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Repository/module structure and source-install docs show kernel/portal/web/webapi/services/deployment areas, Git, Maven, Java 11, and Tomcat. Historical tool criteria document APIs, configuration, database support, clustering, accessibility, and interoperability, but are not current whole-platform architecture evidence.
implementation_evidence: Contributors fork/clone, use feature/issue branches, put Jira keys in branches/commits, open focused pull requests, and use documented merge strategies. CLA requirements apply.
testing_evidence: Pull requests are checked for passing tests; QA verifies resolutions and reopens failed issues. Nightly servers are used for testing; install documentation identifies QA-tested version/tool combinations.
release_or_operations_evidence: Repository and install guide document supported/development versions, release notes, nightly testing, Maven/Tomcat deployment, configuration, and release-manager merges to supported releases.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Private security Jira/repository workflow, Security Working Group/Core Team review, published advisories, and security-only changes for older unsupported versions are documented.
limitations: No explicit SDLC label; evidence is distributed across repositories, Confluence/Jira, and version-specific docs. Some cited criteria are historical/stale; current CI, architecture decisions, coverage, and security SLAs are incomplete publicly.

license_or_model: MIT License; developed with and for the community by Learning Equality
sdlc_model: Gitflow is explicitly documented; lifecycle also includes dev/alpha/beta/final phases, PR review, automated checks, release branches/tags, and release automation.
requirements_evidence: Product approach is explicitly open, transparent, community-based, and needs-driven. Suggestions/bugs enter forums and GitHub; labels and milestones prioritize work from P0 to P3.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Docs describe Python/Django server, SQLite/PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Vue/JavaScript client, core modules, optional plugins, and plugin hooks. Design rules include layered concerns, small interfaces, simple implementations, composition, and behavior-focused tests.
implementation_evidence: Fork/PR workflow against develop; Git LFS, uv, Node 20, pnpm, local/Docker development, migrations, build targets, PR templates, labels, review, and passing checks are documented.
testing_evidence: TDD Red/Green/Refactor guidance; pytest/Django backend tests; Jest/Vue Testing Library frontend tests; tox, linting, link checks, pre-commit, manual testing, Gherkin/UI review, and required passing automated tests.
release_or_operations_evidence: Dev, alpha, beta, final and patch releases use versions, tags, branches, checklists, automation, Buildkite, wheel/DEB/Android repositories, npm/PyPI publishing, OIDC trusted publishing, and SLSA attestations.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Private GitHub Advisory/email reporting, response targets, coordinated 90-day disclosure, published advisories, Sentry, code-quality rules, and maintenance patches are documented.
limitations: Public evidence is incomplete for formal product requirements, sign-off, production monitoring/incident response, dependency governance, and end-of-life policy; documented practice does not prove universal execution.

sdlc_model: Not explicitly stated; TDD-based planning, issue/PR/CI implementation, scheduled QA/deployment, feature gating, regression handling, and privacy review are documented.
requirements_evidence: Technical Design Documents plan features before substantial coding, cover user tasks/stories, testing plans, technical requirements, APIs, database, frontend, privacy, stakeholder feedback, and approval. Issues and starter issues are documented contribution entry points.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Repository documents Python/Angular/Google App Engine. TDD guidance covers high-level and architectural decisions, evaluation criteria, storage models, user flows, controllers/services, API changes, and database design.
implementation_evidence: CLA, setup, issue selection, code/style guidance, PR instructions, develop branch, and TDD implementation plans are documented; backend/frontend work may be split into separate PRs for isolated testing/review.
testing_evidence: Backend, frontend, end-to-end, TypeScript, Lighthouse, Pylint, and ESLint tests are listed. CI uses GitHub Actions, merge queue, local reproduction, and develop-branch comparison. Monthly release QA tests critical user journeys and verifies fixes.
release_or_operations_evidence: Monthly releases are typically cut first Wednesday; QA finishes the following week and final deployment the week after. Release coordinators deploy test/production; feature gating supports controlled exposure.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Security reports go to admin@oppia.org. Privacy-aware programming requires data-flow review in design/implementation. Revert-and-regression policy covers revert/fix-forward, tracking, notification, and preventive tests/lint/review changes.
limitations: No formal SDLC label; public evidence lacks complete requirements lifecycle, deployment infrastructure, vulnerability SLA, security history, and metrics. Some wiki/Google Docs may change over time.

license_or_model: AGPLv3 open-source software; maintained by Instructure
sdlc_model: Not explicitly stated; evidence shows issue/feature intake, focused PRs, automated tests/linting, code/QA/product review, merge, and frequent beta-to-production deploys.
requirements_evidence: GitHub issues are for defects; feature requests go to Canvas Community. Bug reports require summary, reproduction, expected behavior, and context. Roadmap feedback guides product development.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Repository structure separates app/config/migrations/lib/ui/packages/spec/build files. Canvas documents REST/HTTPS/JSON/OAuth2 APIs and OpenAPI generation. CODEOWNERS assigns architecture/service ownership.
implementation_evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md documents master/stable guidance, focused commits, rationale, linked issues, Test Plan, React UI, Ruby/JS/style linting, contributor agreement, and review/merge gates.
testing_evidence: Automated suite, targeted local tests, script/rlint, engineer review, QA test-plan execution, product-manager review for UI/behavior, and exposed spec/Jest/Vitest/Jenkins artifacts are documented.
release_or_operations_evidence: Deploy notes describe two-week deploys for fixes/performance/features, beta testing before production, public release notes, and institution review of custom CSS/JS after deploys.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Private Bugcrowd bug bounty and security@instructure.com reporting are documented. API change logs, recurring deploy notes, bug/performance fixes, and deprecation tracking support maintenance evidence.
limitations: Public repo may not represent proprietary hosted-service practices. No named SDLC model; requirements, architecture decisions, CI thresholds, SRE/rollback, SLOs, vulnerability SLAs, and quantitative QA are not fully public.

sdlc_model: Not explicitly stated; open-source issue/roadmap workflow with branches, pull requests, versioned binary releases, and changelogs.
requirements_evidence: Roadmap lists future release goals. Feature-request template asks for problem, desired solution, alternatives, and context, with educational-use/ease-of-use constraints. Issues accept bugs and features.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Qt desktop application primarily in C++ with JavaScript/HTML/CSS. Source modules cover board/core/gui/network/pdf/web. Web widgets use .wgt and an integrated API. qmake is the official release build path; CMake is community-contributed.
implementation_evidence: Contributor guide documents clone, branch, coding, technical commit notes, issue-linked PRs, source builds, and supported build environments. It states there are no specific coding guidelines.
testing_evidence: Contributors must test thoroughly and compile before submission. Bug template requires reproduction, expected/actual behavior, versions, OS, branch, and hardware details. Changelog records fixes and known issues; no formal public automation/coverage claim is made.
release_or_operations_evidence: Versioned releases/RCs include dates, commits, change notes, contributors, and downloadable assets. README lists stable/dev versions, maintained platforms, installers, and package/build paths.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Roadmap, issues, changelog, releases, platform support, and dependency/Qt fixes show defect maintenance. GitHub reports no SECURITY.md and no published advisories for the cited repository.
limitations: No formal SDLC, governance charter, traceability, architecture decision records, comprehensive CI/test evidence, release sign-off, monitoring, or security policy is public. CMake documentation is explicitly community-contributed.
sources: A How to Guide for New Contributors

category: Education technology: open-source virtual classroom and web-conferencing system
sdlc_model: Official FAQ explicitly documents: Planning -> Design -> Development -> Beta Testing -> Release Candidate -> General Release. It does not label this as Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, or another standard model.
requirements_evidence: Roadmap is driven by online-learning target market and user stories for teacher, student, administrator, support manager, and developer. It prioritizes stability, usability, modularity, code quality, scalability, and API simplicity; FAQ references roadmap/issues/community requests.
design_or_architecture_evidence: Architecture page documents HTML5 React/TypeScript client, WebRTC, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, Akka, FreeSWITCH, mediasoup/SFU, nginx, recording/conversion flows, and a 3.0 restructuring. Design guide documents mobile-first, accessibility, cross-platform, and extensible UI.
implementation_evidence: Development guide covers source modification/compilation, component/package organization, Git/GitHub, docker-dev, issues, design docs for major changes, committer review, and testing committed updates against latest builds.
testing_evidence: Roadmap documents unit/integration/stress-test goals; FAQ requires peer review and testing by other developers; beta testing continues until major bugs are addressed. Public repository exposes GNS3/Playwright test assets.
release_or_operations_evidence: Development moves to Ubuntu beta packages, iterative beta testing, RC monitoring, and general release after stability. Releases are quality-based rather than date-based. Installer docs cover Ubuntu 22.04, SSL/network requirements, bbb-install.sh, upgrades, and bbb-conf --check.
security_or_maintenance_evidence: Security policy documents supported versions and private reporting through GitHub Advisories or security@bigbluebutton.org. API docs describe HTTPS, checksum authentication, and signed JWT callbacks. Roadmap/FAQ document refactoring, stability/usability work, and issue maintenance.
limitations: FAQ lifecycle documentation may be longstanding/versioned; public evidence does not establish current complete CI rules, test coverage, deployment automation, or vulnerability-response SLA.
